text:
kevin: Quick proposal — implement a 'priority fallthrough' routing step so we can run more standard-tier traffic on cheaper preemptible pools while preserving premium SLOs. Thoughts?

maria: Sounds promising. How do you plan to detect imminent evictions so we don't break short-tail latency? :thinking_face:

kevin: Two signals: cloud preemptible-termination notice + our kernel-level page-fault spike heuristic. If either triggers within 15s we mark node as draining for new low-priority requests.

jin: Can we avoid cache-invalidations when we move a request mid-token? KV cache across model variants is brittle.

kevin: Good point. Plan is: prefer regional model-variant fallthroughs that share tokenizer and KV layout. If we must change quantization/architecture, do full restart and stream a graceful error to client.

ops-bot: [deploy] rolling-policy-update started for routing/service: routing-v2 -> v2.1 (canary 5%)

sam: Will this make batching worse for preemptible pools? We already push big batches to save cost.

kevin: Expect slight batching drop for standard-tier because of shorter-lived worker windows. Compensate with adaptive batch_size by estimating time-to-eviction and lowering max_latency target:

```
# pseudo-config
routing:
  tiers:
    premium:
      pools: [reserved, dedicated]
      fallback: [reserved-variant]
    standard:
      pools: [reserved, preemptible]
      fallback: [regional-variant, low-quant]
eviction_buffer_secs: 12
batch_adaptive:
  max_latency_ms: 120
  eviction_penalty_ms: 40
```

lisa: Tradeoffs seem clear. We should also add a cost-leak metric so finance can see delta per-customer if they opt into standard fallthrough.

maria: Also add a per-route cookie to prefer preserved cache if customer pins a model version. If pinned -> skip preemptible.

jin: For canary, suggest route 5% of standard-tier to preemptible for a single region and run for 6h during off-peak, collect p50/p90/p99 and error-rate.

kevin: Agreed. Action items:
- run canary (5% standard, us-west-2) — @ops-bot to schedule
- add eviction buffer telemetry to tracing — @jin
- cost-leak dashboard per-customer — @lisa
- update runbook for mid-token variant fallback — @maria

ops-bot: [sched] canary job created: canary-routing-1812345678 (us-west-2, 5%, 6h)

maria: Small nit: make sure we don't route high-sensitivity customers (HIPAA/PAYMENT) into preemptible even if they're standard-tier. That should be a separate allowlist.

kevin: Yep, adding allowlist. Also proposing a soft-fallback that returns a partial stream with a trailing note when variant fallback occurs: "Note: degraded model variant returned due to capacity; quality may differ."

sam: If eviction buffer is only 12s, can we still finish a 64-token response? Need math: token gen ~70ms/token -> 64 tokens ~4.5s, ok. For long chats (>512 tokens) clients should support resumable streams.

jin: For ops, quick troubleshooting commands:
```
# check nodes in draining state
kubectl get nodes -l state=draining -o wide
# check eviction notice logs
kubectl logs -l app=preempt-watcher --since=15m
```

lisa: I'll add the cost SRD to finance and set a weekly alert if cost-per-req delta > 10% vs baseline.

kevin: Perfect. If no objections I'll start the canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC. :thumbsup:

maria: +1

jin: +1

sam: +1

lisa: +1

ops-bot: [deploy] canary routing-v2.1 started (5% traffic)-> monitor p99, errors, cost

kevin: Thanks everyone. I'll post a follow-up summary with dashboards and the runbook link after the canary starts.
